claims.text: Fabric Data Warehouse is an enterprise-scale relational warehouse built on a data lake foundation, aimed at star/snowflake schemas, curated corporate data marts, and governed semantic models for BI.

Warehouse tables are physically stored as Delta tables (Parquet data files plus a file-based transaction log), the same open format used for all Fabric data, so engineers and business users can share data without separate copies.
Warehouse data is automatically published to OneLake Files in Delta format, making the same tables readable by external engines and other Fabric workloads without export jobs.
Development is primarily in T-SQL on a large SQL Database Engine surface area, including full multi-table ACID transactions, materialized views, functions, and stored procedures.
Storage and compute are separated in the warehouse, which allows near-instant scaling, and workload management is autonomous: the distributed query engine has no user-facing tuning knobs.

A warehouse can be loaded through several routes: the COPY INTO T-SQL command, Data Factory pipelines, Dataflows, Spark bulk writes directly to the Delta tables, or cross-database CTAS / INSERT..SELECT / SELECT INTO statements.
Cross-database queries let a single T-SQL statement combine multiple Fabric data sources in the workspace with zero data duplication.

Every Lakehouse gets an autogenerated SQL analytics endpoint that exposes its Delta tables to T-SQL for read-only querying: you can create views, inline table-valued functions, and procedures and manage object permissions, but you cannot modify the underlying data through it.
Warehouses, Fabric SQL databases, and OneLake all automatically provision a SQL analytics endpoint at creation, built on the same engine technology as the warehouse itself.

Choose a warehouse over a lakehouse when you want enterprise-scale T-SQL-first work over structured or semi-structured data with minimal setup; choose a lakehouse when Spark is the primary tool over heterogeneous, largely unstructured data. Both run the same SQL engine for T-SQL queries, and either can be added later.
Microsoft provides a Fabric Migration Assistant for Data Warehouse to move workloads from Azure Synapse Analytics dedicated SQL pools, SQL Server, and other SQL Database Engine platforms.
